PROPERTY_NAME

Duplicate-aware delivery semantics

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052).

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Declare at-most-once, at-least-once and processing/effect semantics per boundary, including crash, rebalance and replay.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Messages can be lost, duplicated, reordered or redelivered after acknowledgement, visibility timeout or consumer failover.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost work or duplicate processing/effects caused by hidden transport defaults.

MECHANISM

Identify receive, record, commit and external-effect transitions; use transactional processing, duplicate-safe endpoints or reconciliation where the required objective crosses them.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Exactly once for which noun, state and failure envelope?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Processing whose repetition is harmless for the consumer objective over all admitted histories, or one existing atomic local state/message boundary that supplies the required semantics. Self-idempotence of an assignment alone does not cover intervening conflicting intents.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

A declared at-least-once activity or queue can redeliver. An exactly-once internal transition can remain valid despite excluded external calls.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Intent identity, attempt identity and permission/current authority have distinct roles; deduplication does not establish authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State the noun and boundary of at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once semantics and distinguish deliberately new intent.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Journal retention, old-work policy, restore and replay preserve the operation identity contract or explicitly reconcile its limits.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

An acknowledgement establishes its declared boundary, which can include the whole requested effect; missing responses can leave execution unknown.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Prevents delivery labels from being promoted into false business-effect guarantees. Cost: Dedupe state, transaction coordination and reconciliation are paid only for the relevant effect semantics.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Producer, consumer, workflow and effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Do not require an independent second closure for a business effect already atomically enclosed. Do not convert vendor terminology into an unbounded theorem.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: A declared at-least-once activity or queue can redeliver. An exactly-once internal transition can remain valid despite excluded external calls.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Correct the implication that every valid processing boundary necessarily requires a separate business-effect protocol. r2 makes the existing natural-operation alternative explicit over admitted histories and the consumer objective; this propagation clarification is not a separate demonstrated defect in the central proposition.

  2. Dedupe state, transaction coordination and reconciliation are paid only for the relevant effect semantics.

  3. Do not require an independent second closure for a business effect already atomically enclosed. Do not convert vendor terminology into an unbounded theorem.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052). Current adjudication: Correct the implication that every valid processing boundary necessarily requires a separate business-effect protocol. r2 makes the existing natural-operation alternative explicit over admitted histories and the consumer objective; this propagation clarification is not a separate demonstrated defect in the central proposition.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Delivery, processing and effect guarantees apply to named boundaries. Preserve a runtime's useful enclosed guarantee and separately handle only the effects that actually fall outside it.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: Exactly once for which noun, state and failure envelope? Simpler adequate alternative: Processing whose repetition is harmless for the consumer objective over all admitted histories, or one existing atomic local state/message boundary that supplies the required semantics. Self-idempotence of an assignment alone does not cover intervening conflicting intents.

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052).

LINEAGE_CLASS

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Distinguish transport attempts, messages, tasks, workflow steps, business operations and external effects.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

One intent is represented by multiple retries/messages, or one key is reused for semantically changed intent.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate charge/order/action, wrong deduplication, orphan status and unreconcilable effects.

MECHANISM

Bind an intent identifier to appropriate tenant, parameters, result and lifecycle; reject incompatible reuse or represent a deliberately changed intention as a new operation.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Can the receiver distinguish a retry of the same intention from a new intention with the same arguments?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

An update whose repetition is harmless for the consumer objective over all admitted histories, or an enclosed local transaction that already supplies the required identity/effect semantics, can avoid a separate business deduplication service.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

The endpoint interprets and durably enforces the identity. Retention and restore semantics are part of that interpretation.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

ORIGINAL_FORM

Distinguish transport attempts, messages, tasks, workflow steps, business operations and external effects.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

One intent is represented by multiple retries/messages, or one key is reused for semantically changed intent.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Independent components retry and replay without a shared semantic identifier.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate charge/order/action, wrong deduplication, orphan status and unreconcilable effects.

MECHANISM

Assign stable semantic operation ID plus immutable parameter/effect fingerprint; map every attempt/effect; persist status at the authoritative boundary.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Retriable mutation, long-running workflow, external irreversible action or cross-service transaction.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Pure read, locally atomic mutation with no reply-loss concern, or disposable telemetry.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Canonical operation definition, parameter binding, tenant/principal scope, retention and effect ledger/status query.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Provides the join key for idempotency, reconciliation, audit and compensation.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Client, orchestrator, service and external-effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. New ID per retry

  2. Same key reused after parameter change

  3. Key scoped too broadly or narrowly

  4. Effect system drops metadata

  5. Retention expires before replay

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Global identity can cost privacy/cardinality

  2. Canonicalisation is application-specific

  3. Identity alone does not prevent duplicates

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From packet/message identifiers to parameter-bound business intent and effect ledgers.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Identity is semantic and lifecycle-scoped; every attempt and effect is linked without conflating changed intent.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Adding a UUID header is ceremony if semantics, scope and retention are undefined.

PROPERTY_ID

PROPERTY_NAME

Semantic idempotency, not request-ID ritual

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052).

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Repeated execution of the same semantic operation must produce an acceptable state/effect, not merely reuse a key.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A request ID suppresses one duplicate path while downstream, external or changed-parameter effects still repeat.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate payment, email, provision, deletion or state transition despite superficial deduplication.

MECHANISM

Use naturally idempotent operations, an atomic conditional effect/result record, a transactional state transition or an endpoint with an explicit idempotency contract.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: What happens if the worker fails at each boundary between effect and identity recording? Does removal of a repeated attempt preserve the objective when another admitted intent intervenes?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Pure recomputation; one fixed assignment intent with no intervening conflicting mutation; suitable commuting idempotent operations; a correctly scoped version-conditional write; or an existing atomic identity/result boundary or provider contract that already meets the required outcome. Atomic assignment alone does not protect a later superseding intent.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

The same intended operation, parameters, tenant and effect boundary are compared. A crash between effect and separate journal recording can still duplicate the effect. For a journal-free operation, deleting a repeated attempt must preserve the consumer-required outcome over every admitted interleaving. In particular, the same A parameters and identity do not make A:set(1), B:set(2), retry(A):set(1) harmless when B is meant to supersede A.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Intent identity, attempt identity and permission/current authority have distinct roles; deduplication does not establish authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State the noun and boundary of at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once semantics and distinguish deliberately new intent.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Journal retention, old-work policy, restore and replay preserve the operation identity contract or explicitly reconcile its limits.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

An acknowledgement establishes its declared boundary, which can include the whole requested effect; missing responses can leave execution unknown.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes retries safe at the real effect boundary and exposes operations that cannot be made idempotent. Cost: Retained results, coordination and identity governance can outweigh duplicate harm for low-consequence work.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

API owner, workflow author, client and external-effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Idempotency does not establish current authority, timely completion or validity of the first effect. It does not forbid a deliberate second operation. Recognizing an already completed A suppresses its duplicate in that displayed history; it does not order a first arrival of A after B. A latest-intent objective requires its own ordering or version contract.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: The same intended operation, parameters, tenant and effect boundary are compared. A crash between effect and separate journal recording can still duplicate the effect. For a journal-free operation, deleting a repeated attempt must preserve the consumer-required outcome over every admitted interleaving. In particular, the same A parameters and identity do not make A:set(1), B:set(2), retry(A):set(1) harmless when B is meant to supersede A.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Retain semantic duplicate safety with its atomicity and retention premises. r2 corrects the unqualified assignment cheap path under DRF-ADV-001; the central proposition, authority distinction and adequate alternatives remain.

  2. Retained results, coordination and identity governance can outweigh duplicate harm for low-consequence work.

  3. Idempotency does not establish current authority, timely completion or validity of the first effect. It does not forbid a deliberate second operation. Recognizing an already completed A suppresses its duplicate in that displayed history; it does not order a first arrival of A after B. A latest-intent objective requires its own ordering or version contract.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052). Current adjudication: Retain semantic duplicate safety with its atomicity and retention premises. r2 corrects the unqualified assignment cheap path under DRF-ADV-001; the central proposition, authority distinction and adequate alternatives remain.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Duplicate safety is a property of the effect and its declared operation identity, including atomic result recording and restart behavior; assigning an ID alone is insufficient.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: What happens if the worker fails at each boundary between effect and identity recording? Does removal of a repeated attempt preserve the objective when another admitted intent intervenes? Simpler adequate alternative: Pure recomputation; one fixed assignment intent with no intervening conflicting mutation; suitable commuting idempotent operations; a correctly scoped version-conditional write; or an existing atomic identity/result boundary or provider contract that already meets the required outcome. Atomic assignment alone does not protect a later superseding intent.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY

The same intended operation, parameters, tenant and effect boundary are compared. A crash between effect and separate journal recording can still duplicate the effect. For a journal-free operation, deleting a repeated attempt must preserve the consumer-required outcome over every admitted interleaving. In particular, the same A parameters and identity do not make A:set(1), B:set(2), retry(A):set(1) harmless when B is meant to supersede A.

PROPERTY_ID

PROPERTY_NAME

Semantic idempotency, not request-ID ritual

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC duplicate suppression, transaction identifiers, idempotent APIs and durable workflow retries.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Repeated execution of the same semantic operation must produce an acceptable state/effect, not merely reuse a key.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A request ID suppresses one duplicate path while downstream, external or changed-parameter effects still repeat.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Retries, redelivery and late arrivals reach several independently failing effect boundaries.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate payment, email, provision, deletion or state transition despite superficial deduplication.

MECHANISM

Bind identity to semantic parameters; atomically record accepted outcome with effect when possible; make operation naturally idempotent or use guarded state transition/compensation.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any mutation or activity that may be retried, redelivered, replayed or concurrently submitted.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Pure read, commutative accumulation with duplicate identity, or one local transaction.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Operation identity, canonical parameters, current precondition/version, durable result record, downstream closure and retention horizon.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes retries safe at the real effect boundary and exposes operations that cannot be made idempotent.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

API owner, workflow author, client and external-effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Key stored after effect

  2. Key collision across parameters

  3. Downstream call not idempotent

  4. Key window expires too soon

  5. Old success returned after semantics changed

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Natural idempotency is rare for many physical effects

  2. Dedup storage grows

  3. A cached response may hide changed external state

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From duplicate request suppression to semantic equivalence, atomic effect/result recording and end-to-end closure.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

The same operation identity and parameters cannot create more than the allowed semantic effect across retry/restart/replay.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'We add a request ID' is not idempotency.

PROPERTY_ID

PROPERTY_NAME

Bounded deduplication and replay horizon

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052).

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Duplicate suppression remains valid only while identity and result evidence outlive every permitted retry, replay and delayed delivery.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Deduplication records, tombstones, offsets or idempotency keys expire while old work can still arrive.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Ancient duplicate effects, deletion resurrection and false 'new' work after restore.

MECHANISM

Bound admissible age, retain sufficient identity/causal state, reject expired operations or reconcile them under a distinct policy.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Can an admissible old request or restored replica arrive after the evidence needed to interpret it is gone?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Short-lived local transactions with the required operation semantics, or operations whose repetition remains harmless for the consumer objective over all admitted retry/replay histories, can avoid a separate deduplication journal. A fixed assignment is adequate when no intervening conflicting update is admitted.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Backups and migrations do not silently reintroduce an older operation after its distinguishing state was discarded. A time limit is a declared policy, not proof all old messages vanished.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Intent identity, attempt identity and permission/current authority have distinct roles; deduplication does not establish authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State the noun and boundary of at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once semantics and distinguish deliberately new intent.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Journal retention, old-work policy, restore and replay preserve the operation identity contract or explicitly reconcile its limits.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

An acknowledgement establishes its declared boundary, which can include the whole requested effect; missing responses can leave execution unknown.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes exactly-once/effect claims falsifiable in time instead of implicitly permanent. Cost: Storage, privacy, deletion, recovery and metadata-growth costs must be compared with old-work consequences.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Broker/storage owner, API owner, workflow and recovery planner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Infinite retention is not required when the accepted operation contract is bounded. Rejecting old work preserves duplicate safety at a possible completion cost.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: Backups and migrations do not silently reintroduce an older operation after its distinguishing state was discarded. A time limit is a declared policy, not proof all old messages vanished.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Reaffirm the boundary without prescribing a universal duration. r2 makes the existing natural-operation alternative explicit over admitted histories and the consumer objective; this propagation clarification is not a separate demonstrated defect in the central proposition.

  2. Storage, privacy, deletion, recovery and metadata-growth costs must be compared with old-work consequences.

  3. Infinite retention is not required when the accepted operation contract is bounded. Rejecting old work preserves duplicate safety at a possible completion cost.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052). Current adjudication: Reaffirm the boundary without prescribing a universal duration. r2 makes the existing natural-operation alternative explicit over admitted histories and the consumer objective; this propagation clarification is not a separate demonstrated defect in the central proposition.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Finite deduplication or metadata retention must be compatible with the allowed retry, delayed delivery, replay, restore and rejoin horizon, or older work needs an explicit disposition.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: Can an admissible old request or restored replica arrive after the evidence needed to interpret it is gone? Simpler adequate alternative: Short-lived local transactions with the required operation semantics, or operations whose repetition remains harmless for the consumer objective over all admitted retry/replay histories, can avoid a separate deduplication journal. A fixed assignment is adequate when no intervening conflicting update is admitted.

PROPERTY_ID

P20

PROPERTY_NAME

Bounded deduplication and replay horizon

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC duplicate caches, broker retention, event logs and workflow histories.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Duplicate suppression remains valid only while identity and result evidence outlive every permitted retry, replay and delayed delivery.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Deduplication records, tombstones, offsets or idempotency keys expire while old work can still arrive.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Long partitions, restore from old backup, delayed queues and operator replay exceed the assumed window.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Ancient duplicate effects, deletion resurrection and false 'new' work after restore.

MECHANISM

Define maximum retry/replay/rejoin horizon; retain identity/tombstone/result evidence at least that long; reject or manually reconcile older arrivals.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Finite dedup cache, TTL, log retention, replay, delayed replica rejoin or disaster restore.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

No retries/replay and bounded local execution, or effect is naturally harmless under repetition.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

End-to-end maximum delay, restore age, retention policy, compaction rules and explicit post-expiry consequence.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes exactly-once/effect claims falsifiable in time instead of implicitly permanent.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Broker/storage owner, API owner, workflow and recovery planner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Late message after TTL

  2. Old backup resurrects consumed ID

  3. Tombstone compacted before replica returns

  4. Consumer offset retained less than data

  5. Key eviction under load

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Worst-case retention can be expensive

  2. Unbounded partitions make finite guarantees impossible

  3. Legal/business horizons may exceed technical retry windows

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From implementation-local duplicate caches to end-to-end replay-horizon contracts tied to restore and rejoin.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Every dedup/compaction expiry has an explicit maximum-age assumption and behaviour for older arrivals.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A seven-day idempotency window is not a permanent exactly-once guarantee.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE

OPEN_QUESTIONS

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: An ACK proves only the exact durable boundary that emitted it; it does not prove the intended downstream or real-world postcondition.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Callers treat receipt, queue acceptance, worker DONE or DB commit as proof the whole intended action occurred.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False completion, lost external action, duplicate retry and unreconciled partial effects.

MECHANISM

Name the acknowledged boundary and only seek additional evidence for effects the contract excludes.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: What exactly is established by this response, and what required consequence remains outside it?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

The successful return of one local transaction or RPC whose contract encloses the required effect.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

The caller is interpreting the documented response from the correct operation and failure envelope. A queue acceptance is not a remote recipient's action.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Intent identity, attempt identity and permission/current authority have distinct roles; deduplication does not establish authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State the noun and boundary of at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once semantics and distinguish deliberately new intent.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Journal retention, old-work policy, restore and replay preserve the operation identity contract or explicitly reconcile its limits.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

An acknowledgement establishes its declared boundary, which can include the whole requested effect; missing responses can leave execution unknown.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes completion meaningful to the consumer rather than transport-local. Cost: Additional verification can add latency, load and new failure modes without changing a decision already justified by the primary contract.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Caller, orchestrator, business owner and incident responder.

  3. Do not demote every ACK to acceptance-only or require a universal second observer. The native mature proposition already allows consumer-relative completion.

Completion is relative to the consumer's postcondition and the response contract. An acknowledgement may establish durable acceptance, an internal transition or the entire requested operation, depending on that contract.

PROPERTY_NAME

Acknowledgement separated from verified external effect

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

End-to-end arguments, RPC ambiguity, transaction commit records and workflow completion semantics.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

An ACK proves only the exact durable boundary that emitted it; it does not prove the intended downstream or real-world postcondition.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Callers treat receipt, queue acceptance, worker DONE or DB commit as proof the whole intended action occurred.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Effects cross several independent systems and some acknowledgements are lost or emitted before downstream completion.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False completion, lost external action, duplicate retry and unreconciled partial effects.

MECHANISM

Name ACK boundary; link it to operation identity; verify required external postcondition or atomically close/compensate the remaining boundary.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Multi-hop action, asynchronous processing, third-party/physical effect or workflow completion.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Single local transaction whose return covers the entire required state change.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Declared postcondition, authoritative observation, provenance, effect identity and uncertainty/compensation policy.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes completion meaningful to the consumer rather than transport-local.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Caller, orchestrator, business owner and incident responder.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Queue ACK before processing

  2. Worker DONE before durable effect

  3. DB commit before third-party response

  4. Success cached while downstream rolled back

  5. Observation is stale

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Independent verification may be expensive or impossible

  2. Observation can race later reversal

  3. Some effects are only probabilistically observable

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From transport receipt to end-to-end effect evidence and explicit residual uncertainty.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Completion is defined by the consumer's postcondition, with the evidence boundary and remaining uncertainty stated.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A 200 response, broker ACK or worker DONE is not completion by itself.

PROPERTY_NAME

Transactional messaging or outbox/inbox closure

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052).

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Close the atomicity gap between local state change and message publication/consumption.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A service commits state but fails to publish, publishes but rolls back, or applies an effect and crashes before advancing acknowledgement.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost event, duplicate state transition, offset/effect skew and inconsistent downstream projection.

MECHANISM

Persist the intended message with application state, or atomically commit consumed offsets and produced records; make relay and consumer semantics explicit.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Can a crash leave changed state without the message record, or a visible effect without its recovery evidence?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Direct local transaction when no asynchronous handoff is needed; existing enclosed transactional processing.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

All state included in the claim participates in the promised atomic operation. Storage and recovery honor the record; an external sink is included only if its protocol actually joins the closure.

FAILURE_MODEL

Lost requests or replies, redelivery, crash between effect and recording, delayed replay and identity reuse can change the observed outcome.

TIMING_MODEL

Timeout and retention are policy or protocol bounds, not proof of nonexecution or disappearance of every old message.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

An enclosed exactly-once state transition may be valid while a separate external effect lies outside it.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Intent identity, attempt identity and permission/current authority have distinct roles; deduplication does not establish authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State the noun and boundary of at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once semantics and distinguish deliberately new intent.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Journal retention, old-work policy, restore and replay preserve the operation identity contract or explicitly reconcile its limits.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

An acknowledgement establishes its declared boundary, which can include the whole requested effect; missing responses can leave execution unknown.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Creates a recoverable handoff between local atomicity and asynchronous delivery. Cost: Relay backlog, journal cleanup, duplicated deliveries and operational ownership accompany the removed dual-write gap.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service owner, broker/stream operator, projection and workflow.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. An outbox name does not establish endpoint idempotency, business validity or arbitrary external exactly-once behavior.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: All state included in the claim participates in the promised atomic operation. Storage and recovery honor the record; an external sink is included only if its protocol actually joins the closure.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Retain bounded atomic handoff and preserve the useful positive guarantee.

  2. Relay backlog, journal cleanup, duplicated deliveries and operational ownership accompany the removed dual-write gap.

  3. An outbox name does not establish endpoint idempotency, business validity or arbitrary external exactly-once behavior.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

RPC uncertainty and end-to-end responsibility precede transactional log processing and durable workflow contracts (S044,S043,S049,S050,S052). Current adjudication: Retain bounded atomic handoff and preserve the useful positive guarantee.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Atomic state-and-message handoff can prevent a gap inside its defined transaction boundary; delivery after that boundary can still duplicate or fail.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: Can a crash leave changed state without the message record, or a visible effect without its recovery evidence? Simpler adequate alternative: Direct local transaction when no asynchronous handoff is needed; existing enclosed transactional processing.

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Identify exactly which participants and effects commit atomically, and the failure/blocking model of that choice.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Atomicity is assumed across databases, messages and external systems that are not in one commit protocol.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Participant failure, in-doubt commit, intermediate observation, concurrent business actions and compensator failure have different consequences.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Partial commit, contradictory participant outcomes and false rollback expectations.

MECHANISM

Compare local transactions, distributed commit and durable multi-step workflows using participant failures, blocking, intermediate visibility and repair obligations.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Must the invariant hold before external observation, and which design pays the smaller complete lifecycle cost under credible failures?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One local transaction may be both simpler and cheaper even when its business action could be compensated.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Atomic commit covers participating state and the specified recovery model. Skeen's nonblocking result assumes a nonfailing network and reliable failure detection; it is not a partition-tolerant deployment theorem.

FAILURE_MODEL

Participant failure, in-doubt commit, intermediate observation, concurrent business actions and compensator failure have different consequences.

TIMING_MODEL

The invariant may need to hold before observation, or may permit a bounded or explicitly unresolved repair interval; nonblocking results retain their synchrony premises.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Atomic commit, transaction isolation and semantic compensation protect different boundaries; compensatability does not imply atomic commit is inappropriate.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Participants and business actors have authority over particular state; a compensator cannot necessarily undo another actor's later action.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Retries of steps and compensators may duplicate effects unless the selected endpoint contract handles them.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

State the postcondition restored, irreversible consequences, failure handling and accountable unresolved residuals.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Business repair and knowledge of historical execution are recorded separately; intermediate visibility can make an inverse inadequate.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes atomicity real within a defensible boundary and exposes blocking/availability cost. Cost: Locking, messages, in-doubt state and availability compete with compensation, reconciliation, business exposure and human intervention.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Database/application designer, coordinator and recovery operator.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: Atomic commit covers participating state and the specified recovery model. Skeen's nonblocking result assumes a nonfailing network and reliable failure detection; it is not a partition-tolerant deployment theorem.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Correct the native non-compensatable-only selection rule; preserve transaction scope and in-doubt recovery.

  2. Locking, messages, in-doubt state and availability compete with compensation, reconciliation, business exposure and human intervention.

  3. The existence of a compensator does not prove a saga is cheaper or adequate. Weak transaction visibility guarantees do not automatically supply every atomic-commit property.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Database recovery and atomic commitment coexist with semantic sagas rather than forming an unconditional replacement sequence (S017,S018,S019). Current adjudication: Correct the native non-compensatable-only selection rule; preserve transaction scope and in-doubt recovery.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Choose an atomic commit boundary, semantic compensation or another recovery design by the invariant, visibility timing and total cost. Non-compensatability is not a necessary condition for choosing atomic commit.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. PROPERTY_NAME

Explicit transactional boundary and atomic-commit choice

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Transactions, distributed serialisability, two-phase/nonblocking commit and later deterministic/geo transaction systems.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Identify exactly which participants and effects commit atomically, and the failure/blocking model of that choice.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Atomicity is assumed across databases, messages and external systems that are not in one commit protocol.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Coordinator or participant fails between prepare/commit; partitions leave in-doubt participants or partial external effects.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Partial commit, contradictory participant outcomes and false rollback expectations.

MECHANISM

Use local transaction, 2PC/consensus-backed transaction, deterministic ordering or another atomic protocol only for participating resources; persist in-doubt state.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

A non-compensatable invariant requires all-or-nothing across multiple transactional participants.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One local transaction; or independently commit compensatable steps with a durable saga.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Participant durability, coordinator log, isolation, recovery protocol, timeout semantics and explicit exclusion of nonparticipants.

FAILURE_MODEL

Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.

TIMING_MODEL

Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes atomicity real within a defensible boundary and exposes blocking/availability cost.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Database/application designer, coordinator and recovery operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Coordinator log lost

  2. Participant heuristic decision

  3. External effect outside protocol

  4. Prepared transaction blocks resources

  5. Isolation weaker than invariant

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. 2PC can block and add latency

  2. Blanket rejection ignores cases where atomicity is worth cost

  3. Blanket adoption extends scope too far

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From global transaction aspiration to scoped atomicity, replicated coordinators, deterministic ordering and hybrid saga boundaries.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Choose atomic commit for a named non-compensatable closure; otherwise prefer local transactions plus durable handoff/compensation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'ACID' or '2PC' without participant/effect boundary is ceremony.

PROPERTY_ID

PROPERTY_NAME

Durable workflow state as a recoverable distributed state machine

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Persist enough workflow history/state that orchestration survives process loss and resumes deterministically or by explicit repair.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Request/worker memory is lost on restart; timers, child work, retries and compensation become orphaned.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost long-running work, duplicate restart, forgotten timers/compensations and operator guesswork.

MECHANISM

Persist explicit state or replayable history with atomic conditional progress, durable messages and defined retry/recovery behavior.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Which internal states and messages survive interruption, and which visible actions are outside that proof?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One explicit durable state machine or short local transaction instead of a generic workflow platform.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Required storage primitives, deterministic orchestration, worker behavior and retained history satisfy the model. Logical centralization can be valid.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and cancellation may guide reassignment without proving physical cessation; useful completion has a consumer-specific boundary.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Internal observational correctness is separated from external effects and task semantic validity; S052's fault proof excludes external calls and critical sections.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Eligible workers, task attempts and resource acceptance determine who may commit or effect work; workflow identity is not itself sink authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity calls can repeat; internal commit can still occur once. The effect boundary determines the needed duplicate policy.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Each live history retains a compatible eligible execution or migration path; every deployed build need not understand every history.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Record orchestration state, attempt outcomes and required effect evidence without demanding an unnecessary second observer.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes distributed work state recoverable and inspectable rather than implicit in transient processes. Cost: History growth, replay, dependency tracking, storage and platform maintenance can be amortized across many workflows.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow author, orchestration runtime, operator and business owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Internal observational exactly-once does not prove business-effect uniqueness, task semantic validity or current external state. It remains valuable on its own.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: Required storage primitives, deterministic orchestration, worker behavior and retained history satisfy the model. Logical centralization can be valid.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Reaffirm durable execution while retaining paper-version and external-boundary limitations.

  2. History growth, replay, dependency tracking, storage and platform maintenance can be amortized across many workflows.

  3. Internal observational exactly-once does not prove business-effect uniqueness, task semantic validity or current external state. It remains valuable on its own.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms. PROPERTY_ID

P25

PROPERTY_NAME

Durable workflow state as a recoverable distributed state machine

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Sagas, workflow systems, durable logs and modern serverless durable execution.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Persist enough workflow history/state that orchestration survives process loss and resumes deterministically or by explicit repair.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Request/worker memory is lost on restart; timers, child work, retries and compensation become orphaned.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Orchestrator and workers fail independently while tasks and external effects continue.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost long-running work, duplicate restart, forgotten timers/compensations and operator guesswork.

MECHANISM

Persist workflow transitions/history, task identities, timers, signals and terminal state; replay or recover from snapshot/log; expose manual intervention.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Long-running, multi-step, retrying or externally signalled work that must survive process/platform restart.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Synchronous local call/transaction whose whole lifetime fits one reliable execution boundary.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Durable ordered history, stable workflow/run identity, deterministic/versioned orchestration and external-effect reconciliation.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes distributed work state recoverable and inspectable rather than implicit in transient processes.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow author, orchestration runtime, operator and business owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. History lost or corrupted

  2. External effect not in history

  3. Replay code changed

  4. Duplicate task after recovery

  5. Terminal state set before effect verified

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Persistence adds latency/cost

  2. History can grow

  3. Durability does not guarantee semantic correctness of external world

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From ad hoc retry scripts and sagas to durable state machines with history, timers, signals and explicit effect boundaries.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Workflow history is authoritative for orchestration, while external state is independently validated where required.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Deploying a workflow engine is not the property if workflow/effect state is not durable and reconcilable.

PROPERTY_NAME

Task ownership, lease expiry and duplicate-safe re-dispatch

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: A task may be re-dispatched only with a policy for the prior worker that may still be alive and acting.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Heartbeat/lease expires because a worker is slow or partitioned; new worker starts while old worker resumes.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Double execution, conflicting writes, duplicate external side effect and lost progress.

MECHANISM

Use atomic commit preconditions, sink fencing, semantic idempotency or harmless overlap. A compensation policy handles allowed consequences only after establishing that such consequences are acceptable.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: If both attempts run, what prevents or legitimately tolerates their combined effects?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Harmless duplicate computation or a single worker with acceptable downtime.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

The old actor may still run and reach the effect boundary. Cooperative cancellation requires worker participation; termination does not guarantee cleanup.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and cancellation may guide reassignment without proving physical cessation; useful completion has a consumer-specific boundary.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Internal observational correctness is separated from external effects and task semantic validity; S052's fault proof excludes external calls and critical sections.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Eligible workers, task attempts and resource acceptance determine who may commit or effect work; workflow identity is not itself sink authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity calls can repeat; internal commit can still occur once. The effect boundary determines the needed duplicate policy.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Each live history retains a compatible eligible execution or migration path; every deployed build need not understand every history.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Record orchestration state, attempt outcomes and required effect evidence without demanding an unnecessary second observer.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Allows recovery from lost workers without converting slowness into duplicate harm. Cost: Aggressive expiry improves reassignment speed but can create overlap; long expiry delays recovery.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Orchestrator, scheduler, worker and effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. The mere presence of compensation does not make every duplicate or irreversible effect safe. A lease can be sufficient in a narrower bounded model.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: The old actor may still run and reach the effect boundary. Cooperative cancellation requires worker participation; termination does not guarantee cleanup.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Correct compensation-as-safety shorthand while retaining duplicate-safe redispatch.

  2. Aggressive expiry improves reassignment speed but can create overlap; long expiry delays recovery.

  3. The mere presence of compensation does not make every duplicate or irreversible effect safe. A lease can be sufficient in a narrower bounded model.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms. Current adjudication: Correct compensation-as-safety shorthand while retaining duplicate-safe redispatch.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Redispatch after suspected failure must tolerate an old attempt resuming within the required consequence model. Lease or visibility expiry does not physically stop it.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: If both attempts run, what prevents or legitimately tolerates their combined effects? Simpler adequate alternative: Harmless duplicate computation or a single worker with acceptable downtime.

PROPERTY_ID

P26

PROPERTY_NAME

Task ownership, lease expiry and duplicate-safe re-dispatch

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Leases, task queues, workflow activity retries and fencing generations.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

A task may be re-dispatched only with a policy for the prior worker that may still be alive and acting.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Heartbeat/lease expires because a worker is slow or partitioned; new worker starts while old worker resumes.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Two attempts concurrently believe they own one task or external effect.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Double execution, conflicting writes, duplicate external side effect and lost progress.

MECHANISM

Give attempts stable operation identity and attempt generation; fence protected resources or make effects idempotent/compensatable; retain unknown prior attempt state.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Task queue, visibility timeout, worker lease, heartbeat or automatic re-dispatch.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One local worker under a process-local lock, or harmless repeatable calculation with no effect.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Task/run/attempt identity, current ownership generation, timeout policy, effect closure, heartbeat semantics and durable retry record.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Allows recovery from lost workers without converting slowness into duplicate harm.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Orchestrator, scheduler, worker and effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Lease expiry does not stop worker

  2. New attempt uses new operation ID

  3. External sink ignores generation

  4. Heartbeat delayed under overload

  5. Cancellation races completion

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Fencing every external effect can be impossible

  2. Long leases slow recovery

  3. Short leases create false failover

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From visibility timeout/redelivery to generation-bound attempts, unknown-state handling and effect-specific duplicate protection.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Re-dispatch is safe even if the prior actor resumes; the mechanism is fencing, semantic idempotency or explicit compensation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A visibility timeout or heartbeat is not proof the old worker cannot act.

PROPERTY_ID

P27

PROPERTY_NAME

Completion under the declared operation and consumer contract

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: A distributed action is complete only at a declared consumer-relevant postcondition, not merely because a worker returned.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Workflow state says DONE while downstream, external or physical state is absent, stale or later rolled back.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False terminal state, premature notification, duplicate re-execution and unreconciled real-world action.

MECHANISM

Define completion at the operation's authoritative boundary and retain unresolved residuals only where they affect that objective.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: Would the consumer make the same justified decision with the evidence already supplied?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

An atomic operation's normal return when it encloses the complete requested effect.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

A verified internal state can be complete for an internal consumer and insufficient for a different external consumer.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and cancellation may guide reassignment without proving physical cessation; useful completion has a consumer-specific boundary.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Internal observational correctness is separated from external effects and task semantic validity; S052's fault proof excludes external calls and critical sections.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Eligible workers, task attempts and resource acceptance determine who may commit or effect work; workflow identity is not itself sink authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity calls can repeat; internal commit can still occur once. The effect boundary determines the needed duplicate policy.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Each live history retains a compatible eligible execution or migration path; every deployed build need not understand every history.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Record orchestration state, attempt outcomes and required effect evidence without demanding an unnecessary second observer.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Makes DONE auditable and meaningful, preserving uncertainty instead of hiding it. Cost: Extra checks add load and latency; false certainty and endless verification both have costs.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Business process owner, caller, orchestrator and operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Completion need not require an independent external observer, nor perfect knowledge of every system state.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: A verified internal state can be complete for an internal consumer and insufficient for a different external consumer.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Retain consumer-relative completion without adding a universal verification ceremony.

  2. Extra checks add load and latency; false certainty and endless verification both have costs.

  3. Completion need not require an independent external observer, nor perfect knowledge of every system state.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms. Current adjudication: Retain consumer-relative completion without adding a universal verification ceremony.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A completion state identifies the required postcondition and evidence boundary. Partial or unknown state remains explicit when that evidence does not establish the requested result.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: Would the consumer make the same justified decision with the evidence already supplied? Simpler adequate alternative: An atomic operation's normal return when it encloses the complete requested effect.

PROPERTY_ID

P27

PROPERTY_NAME

Completion defined by durable state plus verified postcondition

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

End-to-end correctness, transaction commit semantics, sagas and durable workflow systems.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

A distributed action is complete only at a declared consumer-relevant postcondition, not merely because a worker returned.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Workflow state says DONE while downstream, external or physical state is absent, stale or later rolled back.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker report, orchestrator commit and external observation occur in different failure domains.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False terminal state, premature notification, duplicate re-execution and unreconciled real-world action.

MECHANISM

Define terminal invariant; persist transition; link required effect identities; independently query/observe or transactionally enclose them; record PARTIAL/UNKNOWN when not proved.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Completion drives user notification, billing, next workflow, resource release or irreversible decision.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Local transaction return covers the complete required postcondition.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Consumer-defined postcondition, authoritative evidence source, operation/effect identity, currentness and residual uncertainty policy.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes DONE auditable and meaningful, preserving uncertainty instead of hiding it.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Business process owner, caller, orchestrator and operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Worker report treated as effect proof

  2. Observation is stale

  3. External state changes after check

  4. Terminal state cannot be reopened

  5. One of several effects omitted

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Independent verification costs latency

  2. Some real-world postconditions are not exactly observable

  3. Continuous conditions can later become false

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From process return codes to durable terminal-state contracts with postcondition evidence and explicit uncertainty.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

DONE identifies the evidence and boundary establishing the required effect; otherwise state remains PARTIAL or UNKNOWN.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Green task status is not completion.

CURRENT_STATUS

WORKFLOW_STATE_PROPERTY

EVIDENCE_STRENGTH

VERY_HIGH

  1. S043

  2. S050

  3. S054

  4. S055

CRITICAL_SOURCES

  1. S044

EMPIRICAL_OR_OUTAGE_EVIDENCE

  1. S073

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE

Formal or implementation correctness does not establish that the deployed assumptions, external effects and operational boundary satisfy the claim.

OPEN_QUESTIONS

  1. How should completion be represented for continuous or probabilistic external conditions?

PROPERTY_ID

PROPERTY_NAME

Deterministic replay with explicit workflow/code version evolution

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. HYBRID

ORIGINAL_FORM

Received author's historical reconstruction, retained as an annotation rather than exclusive provenance: Re-executing orchestration logic against recorded history must reproduce compatible decisions, or migration/version logic must deliberately translate it.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Code, dependencies, nondeterministic APIs or schemas change while old histories are replayed.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Non-deterministic replay, stuck histories, duplicate task scheduling and semantic corruption after deployment.

MECHANISM

Record replay inputs and commands, constrain orchestration nondeterminism, route old histories to compatible workers, version branches or migrate state with explicit semantics.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Apply when the consumer question is consequential: For every live history, which eligible worker or migration can execute it, and when may that path be retired?

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Finish short work before cutover or persist explicit current state without replay.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

The dispatch mechanism and worker lifetime honor eligibility; old histories, dependencies and schemas remain available while needed. A migration itself needs a validity argument.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker crash, duplicate attempts, lease expiry, cancellation race, old history, changed code and external-effect uncertainty are distinct.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and cancellation may guide reassignment without proving physical cessation; useful completion has a consumer-specific boundary.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Internal observational correctness is separated from external effects and task semantic validity; S052's fault proof excludes external calls and critical sections.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Eligible workers, task attempts and resource acceptance determine who may commit or effect work; workflow identity is not itself sink authority.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity calls can repeat; internal commit can still occur once. The effect boundary determines the needed duplicate policy.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Each live history retains a compatible eligible execution or migration path; every deployed build need not understand every history.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Record orchestration state, attempt outcomes and required effect evidence without demanding an unnecessary second observer.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Conditional intended payoff, not a measured effect size: Allows durable execution to survive code evolution without rewriting history accidentally. Cost: Pinned old workers, retained dependencies, history storage and migration testing create long-tail maintenance obligations.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow/runtime developer, deployer and recovery operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. It is unnecessary for every deployed build to replay every live history. Determinism under old code does not establish compatibility with changed code.

  2. Violation of the declared guard: The dispatch mechanism and worker lifetime honor eligibility; old histories, dependencies and schemas remain available while needed. A migration itself needs a validity argument.

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Correct the native every-build/all-history quantifier, preserving its own valid pinning mechanism and hybridization prose.

  2. Pinned old workers, retained dependencies, history storage and migration testing create long-tail maintenance obligations.

  3. It is unnecessary for every deployed build to replay every live history. Determinism under old code does not establish compatibility with changed code.

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

Durable workflows combine earlier recovery and messaging ideas with serverless state/history abstractions; S050,S052,S054,S056 and current owner documentation provide differently bounded mechanisms. Current adjudication: Correct the native every-build/all-history quantifier, preserving its own valid pinning mechanism and hybridization prose.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Each live history must have an eligible compatible execution or migration path. Intentionally incompatible builds may coexist when routing, pinning and retirement preserve that path.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Retain the consumer-relevant contract, not a tool name or mandatory format. Evaluate: For every live history, which eligible worker or migration can execute it, and when may that path be retired? Simpler adequate alternative: Finish short work before cutover or persist explicit current state without replay.
