P08 — Semantic conflict resolution beyond replica byte convergence
PROPERTY_ID

P08

PROPERTY_NAME

Semantic conflict resolution beyond replica byte convergence

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Epidemic replication, Dynamo reconciliation, CRDTs and invariant-confluence/hybrid designs.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. REPLICATION_AND_CONSISTENCY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Concurrent updates must merge according to operation semantics and invariants, not merely produce identical bytes.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Partitioned or multi-writer replicas diverge; deterministic convergence can still produce a business-invalid state.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Concurrent writes, delayed replicas and reordering produce conflicts whose resolution is application-sensitive.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost updates, resurrected deletes, negative inventory, broken uniqueness or arbitrary LWW decisions.

MECHANISM

Use application-specific merge, CRDT with stated algebraic conditions, escrow/reservation, or coordinate the non-confluent invariant.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Offline, geo or multi-writer state where concurrent progress is valuable.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One current writer, local transaction or coordination when the invariant is non-confluent.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Operation algebra, identity/tombstone policy, causal metadata, invariant argument and compaction horizon.

FAILURE_MODEL

Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.

TIMING_MODEL

Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Replication messages tolerate duplicate/reorder according to the protocol and retain required version metadata.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Permits available multi-writer progress only where merge semantics are defensible.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Data-type/application owner and replication layer.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. LWW loses causally important update

  2. Tombstone collected before delayed replica returns

  3. CRDT converges to invalid state

  4. Schema change alters merge semantics

  5. Identity collision merges different intents

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. CRDTs do not solve arbitrary invariants

  2. Metadata/tombstones cost storage

  3. Middleware often lacks domain semantics

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From syntactic reconciliation to algebraic convergence plus separate semantic-invariant preservation and selective coordination.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Prove or test merge/invariant compatibility; otherwise use ownership, reservation or coordination.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'Eventually all replicas match' is not the property if the matched state is wrong.

P09 — Anti-entropy, convergence and repair with corruption/lag safeguards
PROPERTY_ID

P09

PROPERTY_NAME

Anti-entropy, convergence and repair with corruption/lag safeguards

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Epidemic database maintenance, read repair/anti-entropy, log catch-up and CRDT replication.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. REPLICATION_AND_CONSISTENCY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Detect and repair divergence after disconnection or partial write without blindly spreading bad state.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Replicas remain stale indefinitely; repair selects an obsolete/corrupt source or overloads foreground work.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Long-disconnected or corrupted replicas rejoin and exchange state under uncertain currentness.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Silent stale failover, data loss, resurrection or corruption propagation.

MECHANISM

Use version/digest comparison, authorised source selection, integrity/semantic validation, rate-limited repair and guarded rejoin.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Eventually or asynchronously replicated state with a lag/disconnected-replica path.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Synchronous replicated object with no lag path, or immutable artefact verified at write time.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Stable identity/version, current membership, repair-source policy, integrity checks, capacity budget and tombstone horizon.

FAILURE_MODEL

Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.

TIMING_MODEL

Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Replication messages tolerate duplicate/reorder according to the protocol and retain required version metadata.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Restores intended redundancy and consistency without turning repair into a new failure amplifier.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Storage/replication operator and failover controller.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Read repair copies corruption

  2. Repair saturates foreground capacity

  3. Replica catches up from stale source

  4. Deleted data resurrects

  5. Obsolete member rejoins

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. No inherent convergence deadline

  2. Checksums show difference, not correct source

  3. Repair can create metastable overload

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From blind background copying to fenced, integrity-aware, capacity-bounded repair workflows.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Repair has source authority, bounded resource use, rejoin gates and post-repair semantic/integrity validation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Running a periodic repair command is ceremony unless authority and result are established.

P10 — Quorum validity bound to current membership and configuration
PROPERTY_ID

P10

PROPERTY_NAME

Quorum validity bound to current membership and configuration

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Weighted voting, Paxos-family quorums, consensus and strongly consistent databases.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. REPLICATION_AND_CONSISTENCY_LINEAGE

  2. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

An intersecting decision set is meaningful only relative to the same legitimate configuration and state/version.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A numeric majority forms from the wrong, stale, duplicated or non-independent member set.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Partitions and reconfiguration allow conflicting views of who may vote or serve state.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Two configurations each forming majority, stale state winning or restored identity voting twice.

MECHANISM

Version membership; bind votes to term/configuration/log position; preserve intersection through reconfiguration; validate durable identities and placement.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Replicated decision, leader election, lock service or strong database read/write.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One current durable owner or local transaction.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Authoritative configuration identity, unique durable member ID, persisted vote/log and proven transitional overlap.

FAILURE_MODEL

Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.

TIMING_MODEL

Safety and liveness assumptions are separated; progress usually relies on partial synchrony and a reachable quorum.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Agreement/order does not itself establish application semantic validity.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Terms, views, ballots, configurations and durable member identity bind every decision and mutation.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Protocol messages are term/configuration bound and stale messages are rejected.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents majority folklore from masking split authority.

P11 — Consensus safety separated from liveness and semantic validity
PROPERTY_ID

P11

PROPERTY_NAME

Consensus safety separated from liveness and semantic validity

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

FLP, partial synchrony, failure detectors, state-machine replication, Viewstamped Replication, Paxos and Raft.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Agreement/non-divergence, progress/termination and validity of the chosen value are distinct obligations.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A protocol remains safe but unavailable, or all replicas agree on a syntactically valid yet semantically wrong value.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Partitions, slow links and failures prevent progress while agreement remains intact; agreement can choose bad input.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Unsafe manual fail-open, false continuous-availability claim or consensus-as-business-oracle.

MECHANISM

State safety invariant, liveness assumptions and input/application validity separately; expose quorum loss rather than violating safety.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Replicated exclusive decision or ordered log whose divergence would violate an invariant.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Local durable owner, commutative/partitionable state or explicit manual arbitration.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Fault/timing model, durable vote/log, membership, deterministic application and input validation.

FAILURE_MODEL

Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.

TIMING_MODEL

Safety and liveness assumptions are separated; progress usually relies on partial synchrony and a reachable quorum.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Agreement/order does not itself establish application semantic validity.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Terms, views, ballots, configurations and durable member identity bind every decision and mutation.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Protocol messages are term/configuration bound and stale messages are rejected.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Provides replicated decisions without pretending to guarantee continuous availability or semantic correctness.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Protocol implementer, state-machine validator and operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Liveness stalls under partition

  2. Manual dual-primary violates safety

  3. Nondeterministic state machine

  4. Invalid command agreed

  5. Snapshot omits term/vote metadata

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Consensus is overused

  2. Leader implementations can bottleneck

  3. Proofs may not cover storage/reconfiguration/integration bugs

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From 'elect a leader' folklore to separate safety, liveness, validity and implementation evidence.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Use consensus only for a named invariant; preserve safety during lost progress; validate values and deployment assumptions separately.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A leader dashboard is not the property.

P12 — Versioned membership and safe reconfiguration
PROPERTY_ID

P12

PROPERTY_NAME

Versioned membership and safe reconfiguration

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Virtual synchrony/views, Viewstamped Replication, Paxos/Raft reconfiguration and Vertical Paxos.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Membership change is a distributed state transition requiring continuity of authority and quorum intersection.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Nodes join, leave, rebuild or move while old messages, leaders and configurations remain live.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Multiple configurations remain actionable across partition, delayed messaging or restore.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Split brain, two quorums, data loss during replacement or resurrected stale member.

MECHANISM

Use configuration versions/epochs, joint/overlap or equivalent transition, catch-up before voting and retirement/fencing of old identities.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Dynamic replica set, shard movement, autoscaling or disaster rebuild participating in authority.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Static single owner or whole-system offline replacement under an exclusive boundary.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Unique durable identity, configuration log, state transfer/catch-up, overlap proof and operator-visible transition.

FAILURE_MODEL

Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.

TIMING_MODEL

Safety and liveness assumptions are separated; progress usually relies on partial synchrony and a reachable quorum.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Agreement/order does not itself establish application semantic validity.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Terms, views, ballots, configurations and durable member identity bind every decision and mutation.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Protocol messages are term/configuration bound and stale messages are rejected.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Allows elasticity and maintenance without invalidating quorum/consensus assumptions.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Cluster manager, operator and shard/replica controller.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Too many members removed at once

  2. Joining member votes before catch-up

  3. Old identity reused

  4. Config state restored behind data

  5. Control and data planes disagree

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Safe reconfiguration can reduce availability

  2. Tooling often bypasses protocol

  3. Proofs assume reliable identity/storage

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From static groups to logged, epoch-bound, jointly safe reconfiguration.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Membership is authoritative replicated state; decisions and mutations carry configuration/epoch through handoff.

Editing a node list or scaling a controller is not safe reconfiguration.

P13 — Current mutation authority enforced by epochs or fencing
PROPERTY_ID

P13

PROPERTY_NAME

Current mutation authority enforced by epochs or fencing

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Views, terms, ballots, lease-based lock services and fencing-token practice.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

  2. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

Once-valid leadership, lock or lease must not permit mutation after authority transfers.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

An old leader or worker pauses/partitions, a new owner is chosen, then the old actor resumes.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Stale actors remain live and delayed writes arrive after handoff.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Split-brain mutation, duplicate external action, corruption during failover or concurrent maintenance.

MECHANISM

Issue a monotone generation/epoch; attach it to each mutation; protected resource atomically rejects stale generations.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Exclusive writer, task lease, distributed lock, failover, shard ownership or maintenance handoff.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Local mutex/process ownership; commutative operation; local transaction with version check.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Durable monotone generation, resource-side compare/reject, ownership-transfer protocol and effect identity.

FAILURE_MODEL

Crash-recovery, network partition, delayed/stale messages, duplicated identity, reconfiguration and—only when declared—arbitrary faults.

TIMING_MODEL

Safety and liveness assumptions are separated; progress usually relies on partial synchrony and a reachable quorum.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Agreement/order does not itself establish application semantic validity.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Terms, views, ballots, configurations and durable member identity bind every decision and mutation.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Protocol messages are term/configuration bound and stale messages are rejected.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Votes, log position, snapshots and configuration state survive restart without rollback of authority.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Current term, configuration, quorum and commit position can be reconstructed.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Converts advisory ownership into enforceable non-stale mutation safety.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Lock service, scheduler, storage/API owner and failover controller.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Resource ignores token

  2. Generation rolls back on restore

  3. External side effect cannot be fenced

  4. Actor obtains new token for old intent

  5. Multi-resource action fences only one sink

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Every sink must cooperate

  2. Physical/third-party effects may not accept tokens

  3. Authority service can be unavailable

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From leases and locks to end-to-end resource-enforced fencing and versioned handoff.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Authority evidence travels to every effect boundary; stale attempts are rejected or semantically neutralised.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Owning a lock object or seeing oneself as leader is not the property.

P14 — Single-writer or local-transaction cheap path
PROPERTY_ID

P14

PROPERTY_NAME

Single-writer or local-transaction cheap path

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Primary-copy and local transaction lineages, retained as an anti-overengineering conclusion.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. REPLICATION_AND_CONSISTENCY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

Eliminate unnecessary distributed concurrency by placing an invariant under one current durable owner or one local transaction.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Distribution is introduced without a scale, latency, autonomy or availability consumer.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Remote uncertainty, coordination and recovery machinery are created where local atomicity would suffice.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Consensus/commit failure and coordination debt exceeding any benefit.

MECHANISM

Co-locate state and operation; use one durable writer/local atomicity; replicate behind the writer only if needed.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Low write scale, central invariant, tightly coupled data, modest availability demand or easy recovery.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

This property is the cheap path; distribution triggers only after a concrete consumer appears.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Clear ownership, local durability, tested backup and fenced promotion if automatic failover exists.

FAILURE_MODEL

Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.

TIMING_MODEL

Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Replica set, writer authority and configuration identity are current and durable.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Replication messages tolerate duplicate/reorder according to the protocol and retain required version metadata.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Reduces state space, remote unknown outcomes and operational burden.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Architect and application/data owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Owner becomes bottleneck

  2. Failover lacks fencing

  3. Local durability insufficient

  4. Async replicas lose accepted writes

  5. Ownership hidden behind load balancer

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Centralisation may fail latency/availability goals

  2. Future scaling can be difficult

  3. One process is not automatically durable

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From primary-copy replication to an explicit design-first cheap path.

P15 — Strong coordination for non-confluent invariants
PROPERTY_ID

P15

PROPERTY_NAME

Strong coordination for non-confluent invariants

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Distributed serialisability, atomic commit, consensus and invariant-confluence analysis.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  2. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

  3. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Coordinate operations whose independent execution can jointly violate a named invariant.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Locally valid concurrent decisions violate global uniqueness, conservation, bounds or exclusive ownership.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Partitioned or concurrent actors each act on incomplete state and jointly break the invariant.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Double allocation, oversell, duplicate uniqueness, inconsistent atomic transition or divergent ownership.

MECHANISM

Use serialisable transaction, consensus, conditional write, reservation/escrow or authoritative sequencer over the minimal invariant boundary.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Demonstrated non-confluence, globally scarce resource or irreversible action requiring an exclusive current decision.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Independent commutative operations, ownership partitioning, escrowed budgets or one local owner.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Invariant definition, operation set, consistency target, current authority/membership, failure and recovery model.

FAILURE_MODEL

Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.

TIMING_MODEL

Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Preserves a real invariant while containing coordination cost.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Application/data owner and the consumer harmed by invariant violation.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Invariant boundary incomplete

  2. External side effect outside transaction

  3. Global lock bottleneck

  4. Availability fallback violates invariant

  5. Consensus agrees on invalid input

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Coordination hurts latency/availability

  2. Some invariants can be redesigned or escrowed

  3. Blanket 2PC/consensus overcoordinates

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From global transactions and locks to invariant-scoped coordination and hybrid strong/weak designs.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Demonstrate non-confluence, then coordinate the smallest state/effect closure or redesign the operation.

Consensus everywhere is ceremony; invariant-scoped coordination is the property.

PROPERTY_ID

P16

PROPERTY_NAME

Coordination avoidance for invariant-confluent, commutative or partitionable operations

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

CRDT, highly available transaction and invariant-confluence lineages.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. REPLICATION_AND_CONSISTENCY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

Allow independent progress when all valid independently produced states merge without violating the invariant.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Global coordination is used even though operations commute, are ownership-partitioned, escrow-bounded or merge safely.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Unnecessary cross-node coordination turns delay/partition into availability and latency cost.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Avoidable quorum waits, global bottlenecks and lost availability.

MECHANISM

Prove or test invariant confluence/commutativity; use CRDT, escrow/reservation, monotonic dataflow or partition ownership; coordinate only the non-confluent subset.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

High-latency or partitioned environment where operation semantics support safe independent execution.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Non-confluent uniqueness/conservation/exclusive authority or irreversible global effects should coordinate instead.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Operation algebra, merge rule, invariant, duplicate/reorder semantics, metadata retention and ownership boundaries.

FAILURE_MODEL

Replica divergence, stale reads, concurrent writes, partition, corruption, repair error, common-mode failure and obsolete membership.

Availability and convergence may be asynchronous; bounded staleness requires a separate bound and measurement.

The replica model, permitted anomalies, convergence rule and semantic invariant are explicit.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Catch-up, repair, rejoin, compaction and corruption handling are tested.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Lag, divergence, repair source, membership and invariant checks are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Improves availability, latency and scale without sacrificing the named invariant.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Data/application designer and geo/offline client.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Incorrect confluence argument

  2. Hidden cross-object invariant

  3. Metadata collection breaks merge

  4. Schema change breaks commutativity

  5. External effect is non-commutative

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Application semantics are hard to formalise

  2. Complexity can move into reconciliation

  3. Not every converged state is meaningful

P17 — Duplicate-aware delivery semantics
PROPERTY_ID

P17

PROPERTY_NAME

Duplicate-aware delivery semantics

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC retransmission/duplicate suppression, durable logs, stream processing and broker semantics.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Declare at-most-once, at-least-once and processing/effect semantics per boundary, including crash, rebalance and replay.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Messages can be lost, duplicated, reordered or redelivered after acknowledgement, visibility timeout or consumer failover.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Producer, broker and consumer fail independently; acknowledgement and state updates are separated.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost work or duplicate processing/effects caused by hidden transport defaults.

MECHANISM

Define attempt and event identity; persist acknowledgement/offset relative to state; design retry, poison and replay paths; make duplicates safe or explicit.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Asynchronous transfer, queue, event log, task dispatch or producer/consumer retry.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Direct local call/transaction or fire-and-forget telemetry where loss is accepted.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Durable event identity, producer/consumer state, retention, ordering partition and failure/rebalance semantics.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Prevents delivery labels from being promoted into false business-effect guarantees.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Producer, consumer, workflow and effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Ack lost after processing

  2. Offset committed before effect

  3. Effect committed before offset

  4. Duplicate outside dedup window

  5. Partition order mistaken for global order

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. At-most-once may lose work

  2. At-least-once shifts burden to consumer

  3. Platform-scoped exactly-once can be costly and narrow

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From transport retry semantics to end-to-end processing/effect contracts and transactional offset-state integration.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Name semantics at every boundary and independently close the business-effect boundary.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A broker checkbox labelled exactly-once is not an end-to-end guarantee.

CURRENT_STATUS

DELIVERY_IDEMPOTENCY_PROPERTY

P18 — End-to-end business-operation and effect identity
PROPERTY_ID

P18

PROPERTY_NAME

End-to-end business-operation and effect identity

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

End-to-end argument, RPC/request identity, transaction-log and workflow lineages.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

Distinguish transport attempts, messages, tasks, workflow steps, business operations and external effects.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

One intent is represented by multiple retries/messages, or one key is reused for semantically changed intent.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Independent components retry and replay without a shared semantic identifier.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate charge/order/action, wrong deduplication, orphan status and unreconcilable effects.

MECHANISM

Assign stable semantic operation ID plus immutable parameter/effect fingerprint; map every attempt/effect; persist status at the authoritative boundary.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Retriable mutation, long-running workflow, external irreversible action or cross-service transaction.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Pure read, locally atomic mutation with no reply-loss concern, or disposable telemetry.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Canonical operation definition, parameter binding, tenant/principal scope, retention and effect ledger/status query.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Provides the join key for idempotency, reconciliation, audit and compensation.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Client, orchestrator, service and external-effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. New ID per retry

  2. Same key reused after parameter change

  3. Key scoped too broadly or narrowly

  4. Effect system drops metadata

  5. Retention expires before replay

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Global identity can cost privacy/cardinality

  2. Canonicalisation is application-specific

  3. Identity alone does not prevent duplicates

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From packet/message identifiers to parameter-bound business intent and effect ledgers.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Identity is semantic and lifecycle-scoped; every attempt and effect is linked without conflating changed intent.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Adding a UUID header is ceremony if semantics, scope and retention are undefined.

P19 — Semantic idempotency, not request-ID ritual
PROPERTY_ID

P19

PROPERTY_NAME

Semantic idempotency, not request-ID ritual

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC duplicate suppression, transaction identifiers, idempotent APIs and durable workflow retries.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Repeated execution of the same semantic operation must produce an acceptable state/effect, not merely reuse a key.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A request ID suppresses one duplicate path while downstream, external or changed-parameter effects still repeat.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Retries, redelivery and late arrivals reach several independently failing effect boundaries.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Duplicate payment, email, provision, deletion or state transition despite superficial deduplication.

MECHANISM

Bind identity to semantic parameters; atomically record accepted outcome with effect when possible; make operation naturally idempotent or use guarded state transition/compensation.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Any mutation or activity that may be retried, redelivered, replayed or concurrently submitted.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Pure read, commutative accumulation with duplicate identity, or one local transaction.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Operation identity, canonical parameters, current precondition/version, durable result record, downstream closure and retention horizon.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes retries safe at the real effect boundary and exposes operations that cannot be made idempotent.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

API owner, workflow author, client and external-effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Key stored after effect

  2. Key collision across parameters

  3. Downstream call not idempotent

  4. Key window expires too soon

  5. Old success returned after semantics changed

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Natural idempotency is rare for many physical effects

  2. Dedup storage grows

  3. A cached response may hide changed external state

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From duplicate request suppression to semantic equivalence, atomic effect/result recording and end-to-end closure.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

The same operation identity and parameters cannot create more than the allowed semantic effect across retry/restart/replay.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'We add a request ID' is not idempotency.

P20 — Bounded deduplication and replay horizon
PROPERTY_ID

P20

PROPERTY_NAME

Bounded deduplication and replay horizon

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC duplicate caches, broker retention, event logs and workflow histories.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Duplicate suppression remains valid only while identity and result evidence outlive every permitted retry, replay and delayed delivery.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Deduplication records, tombstones, offsets or idempotency keys expire while old work can still arrive.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Long partitions, restore from old backup, delayed queues and operator replay exceed the assumed window.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Ancient duplicate effects, deletion resurrection and false 'new' work after restore.

MECHANISM

Define maximum retry/replay/rejoin horizon; retain identity/tombstone/result evidence at least that long; reject or manually reconcile older arrivals.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Finite dedup cache, TTL, log retention, replay, delayed replica rejoin or disaster restore.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

No retries/replay and bounded local execution, or effect is naturally harmless under repetition.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

End-to-end maximum delay, restore age, retention policy, compaction rules and explicit post-expiry consequence.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes exactly-once/effect claims falsifiable in time instead of implicitly permanent.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Broker/storage owner, API owner, workflow and recovery planner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Late message after TTL

  2. Old backup resurrects consumed ID

  3. Tombstone compacted before replica returns

  4. Consumer offset retained less than data

  5. Key eviction under load

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Worst-case retention can be expensive

  2. Unbounded partitions make finite guarantees impossible

  3. Legal/business horizons may exceed technical retry windows

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From implementation-local duplicate caches to end-to-end replay-horizon contracts tied to restore and rejoin.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Every dedup/compaction expiry has an explicit maximum-age assumption and behaviour for older arrivals.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A seven-day idempotency window is not a permanent exactly-once guarantee.

P21 — Acknowledgement separated from verified external effect
PROPERTY_ID

P21

PROPERTY_NAME

Acknowledgement separated from verified external effect

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

End-to-end arguments, RPC ambiguity, transaction commit records and workflow completion semantics.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

An ACK proves only the exact durable boundary that emitted it; it does not prove the intended downstream or real-world postcondition.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Callers treat receipt, queue acceptance, worker DONE or DB commit as proof the whole intended action occurred.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Effects cross several independent systems and some acknowledgements are lost or emitted before downstream completion.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False completion, lost external action, duplicate retry and unreconciled partial effects.

MECHANISM

Name ACK boundary; link it to operation identity; verify required external postcondition or atomically close/compensate the remaining boundary.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Multi-hop action, asynchronous processing, third-party/physical effect or workflow completion.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Single local transaction whose return covers the entire required state change.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Declared postcondition, authoritative observation, provenance, effect identity and uncertainty/compensation policy.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes completion meaningful to the consumer rather than transport-local.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Caller, orchestrator, business owner and incident responder.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Queue ACK before processing

  2. Worker DONE before durable effect

  3. DB commit before third-party response

  4. Success cached while downstream rolled back

  5. Observation is stale

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Independent verification may be expensive or impossible

  2. Observation can race later reversal

  3. Some effects are only probabilistically observable

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From transport receipt to end-to-end effect evidence and explicit residual uncertainty.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Completion is defined by the consumer's postcondition, with the evidence boundary and remaining uncertainty stated.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A 200 response, broker ACK or worker DONE is not completion by itself.

P22 — Transactional messaging or outbox/inbox closure
PROPERTY_ID

P22

PROPERTY_NAME

Transactional messaging or outbox/inbox closure

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Transaction logs, reliable messaging, stream-processing checkpoint/offset integration and outbox/inbox practice.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  3. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Close the atomicity gap between local state change and message publication/consumption.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

A service commits state but fails to publish, publishes but rolls back, or applies an effect and crashes before advancing acknowledgement.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Database and broker fail independently; network/retry separates commit from message acknowledgement.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost event, duplicate state transition, offset/effect skew and inconsistent downstream projection.

MECHANISM

Atomically write state plus outbox, or transactionally commit broker records/offsets and local state; consumers use inbox/dedup and replay.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

A local transaction must reliably cause or record an asynchronous message, or a consumed event must update state exactly once within the closure.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Direct local state change with no asynchronous notification requirement.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Stable event identity, publisher relay/recovery, ordering assumptions, dedup horizon and explicit external-effect boundary.

FAILURE_MODEL

Message loss, duplication, reordering, redelivery, acknowledgement loss, producer/consumer crash, rebalance and late replay.

TIMING_MODEL

Asynchronous delay is possible; visibility timeouts and retry deadlines are policy bounds, not outcome proofs.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

State/effect and acknowledgement/offset atomicity are explicit where claimed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Producer/consumer/task ownership generations are current for ordered or exclusive processing.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transport attempt, message, processing, business operation and external effect identities are distinct.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Replay, poison handling, dedup retention and unknown outcomes survive restart.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Attempts, duplicates, redeliveries, lag, acknowledgement boundary and effect status are observable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Creates a recoverable handoff between local atomicity and asynchronous delivery.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service owner, broker/stream operator, projection and workflow.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Outbox relay publishes duplicates

  2. Consumer effect outside transaction

  3. Event order differs from state order

  4. Outbox never drained

  5. Schema evolution breaks replay

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Adds storage/relay complexity

  2. Still not atomic with arbitrary third parties

  3. Ordering across partitions is limited

P23 — Explicit transactional boundary and atomic-commit choice
PROPERTY_ID

P23

PROPERTY_NAME

Explicit transactional boundary and atomic-commit choice

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Transactions, distributed serialisability, two-phase/nonblocking commit and later deterministic/geo transaction systems.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  2. DISTRIBUTED_DATABASE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Identify exactly which participants and effects commit atomically, and the failure/blocking model of that choice.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Atomicity is assumed across databases, messages and external systems that are not in one commit protocol.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Coordinator or participant fails between prepare/commit; partitions leave in-doubt participants or partial external effects.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Partial commit, contradictory participant outcomes and false rollback expectations.

MECHANISM

Use local transaction, 2PC/consensus-backed transaction, deterministic ordering or another atomic protocol only for participating resources; persist in-doubt state.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

A non-compensatable invariant requires all-or-nothing across multiple transactional participants.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One local transaction; or independently commit compensatable steps with a durable saga.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Participant durability, coordinator log, isolation, recovery protocol, timeout semantics and explicit exclusion of nonparticipants.

FAILURE_MODEL

Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.

TIMING_MODEL

Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes atomicity real within a defensible boundary and exposes blocking/availability cost.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Database/application designer, coordinator and recovery operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Coordinator log lost

  2. Participant heuristic decision

  3. External effect outside protocol

  4. Prepared transaction blocks resources

  5. Isolation weaker than invariant

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. 2PC can block and add latency

  2. Blanket rejection ignores cases where atomicity is worth cost

  3. Blanket adoption extends scope too far

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From global transaction aspiration to scoped atomicity, replicated coordinators, deterministic ordering and hybrid saga boundaries.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Choose atomic commit for a named non-compensatable closure; otherwise prefer local transactions plus durable handoff/compensation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'ACID' or '2PC' without participant/effect boundary is ceremony.

P24 — Compensation and forward recovery with semantic limits
PROPERTY_ID

P24

PROPERTY_NAME

Compensation and forward recovery with semantic limits

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Sagas and long-running transaction practice, later durable workflow systems.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. DISTRIBUTED_TRANSACTION_LINEAGE

  2. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Recover a long-running distributed operation through ordered compensating or forward actions when global rollback is unavailable.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Steps commit independently and some effects cannot be transactionally rolled back.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Later step fails after earlier durable/internal/external effects; compensation can also fail or be non-inverse.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Permanent unowned partial business state and false claim that rollback restores the past.

MECHANISM

Persist saga state; define compensations/reservations/semantic locks; order and retry them safely; use forward recovery when reversal is impossible; escalate residuals.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Long-running, cross-service or external workflow whose effects are compensatable or repairable but not globally atomic.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One atomic local/distributed transaction when the whole closure can and should commit together.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Effect identity, compensation semantics, ordering, duplicate safety, durable orchestration, current external-state observation and manual path.

FAILURE_MODEL

Concurrent updates, coordinator/participant crash, partition, partial commit, blocked in-doubt state, duplicate side effect and failed compensation.

TIMING_MODEL

Blocking and latency under partition/long-running work are explicit; timeout does not resolve atomic outcome.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Atomicity/isolation covers only the declared transaction boundary; external effects need another closure.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Participants/coordinator/owners and transaction generation are durable and current.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Transaction messages and external calls have stable identity and duplicate-safe recovery.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Coordinator logs, participant states, compensation/forward-recovery ordering and manual resolution are durable.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Prepared/in-doubt/committed/compensating states and unresolved external effects are discoverable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Provides a governed recovery path for partial effects without pretending compensation is a true inverse.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow/business owner, service teams and operations.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Compensation is not inverse

  2. Compensation order wrong

  3. Compensation itself duplicates/fails

  4. External state changed meanwhile

  5. Irreversible effect remains

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Sagas expose intermediate state

  2. Compensations demand domain knowledge

  3. Complexity may exceed a scoped transaction

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From named compensating transactions to durable, observable, idempotent compensation/forward-recovery plans with residual-state handling.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Compensation states what it restores, what it cannot restore and how unresolved residuals are detected and escalated.

P25 — Durable workflow state as a recoverable distributed state machine
PROPERTY_ID

P25

PROPERTY_NAME

Durable workflow state as a recoverable distributed state machine

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Sagas, workflow systems, durable logs and modern serverless durable execution.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. FAULT_TOLERANCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Persist enough workflow history/state that orchestration survives process loss and resumes deterministically or by explicit repair.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Request/worker memory is lost on restart; timers, child work, retries and compensation become orphaned.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Orchestrator and workers fail independently while tasks and external effects continue.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Lost long-running work, duplicate restart, forgotten timers/compensations and operator guesswork.

MECHANISM

Persist workflow transitions/history, task identities, timers, signals and terminal state; replay or recover from snapshot/log; expose manual intervention.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Long-running, multi-step, retrying or externally signalled work that must survive process/platform restart.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Synchronous local call/transaction whose whole lifetime fits one reliable execution boundary.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Durable ordered history, stable workflow/run identity, deterministic/versioned orchestration and external-effect reconciliation.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes distributed work state recoverable and inspectable rather than implicit in transient processes.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow author, orchestration runtime, operator and business owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. History lost or corrupted

  2. External effect not in history

  3. Replay code changed

  4. Duplicate task after recovery

  5. Terminal state set before effect verified

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Persistence adds latency/cost

  2. History can grow

  3. Durability does not guarantee semantic correctness of external world

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From ad hoc retry scripts and sagas to durable state machines with history, timers, signals and explicit effect boundaries.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Workflow history is authoritative for orchestration, while external state is independently validated where required.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Deploying a workflow engine is not the property if workflow/effect state is not durable and reconcilable.

CURRENT_STATUS

WORKFLOW_STATE_PROPERTY

P26 — Task ownership, lease expiry and duplicate-safe re-dispatch
PROPERTY_ID

P26

PROPERTY_NAME

Task ownership, lease expiry and duplicate-safe re-dispatch

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Leases, task queues, workflow activity retries and fencing generations.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONSENSUS_AND_MEMBERSHIP_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

A task may be re-dispatched only with a policy for the prior worker that may still be alive and acting.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Heartbeat/lease expires because a worker is slow or partitioned; new worker starts while old worker resumes.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Two attempts concurrently believe they own one task or external effect.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Double execution, conflicting writes, duplicate external side effect and lost progress.

MECHANISM

Give attempts stable operation identity and attempt generation; fence protected resources or make effects idempotent/compensatable; retain unknown prior attempt state.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Task queue, visibility timeout, worker lease, heartbeat or automatic re-dispatch.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

One local worker under a process-local lock, or harmless repeatable calculation with no effect.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Task/run/attempt identity, current ownership generation, timeout policy, effect closure, heartbeat semantics and durable retry record.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Allows recovery from lost workers without converting slowness into duplicate harm.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Orchestrator, scheduler, worker and effect owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Lease expiry does not stop worker

  2. New attempt uses new operation ID

  3. External sink ignores generation

  4. Heartbeat delayed under overload

  5. Cancellation races completion

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Fencing every external effect can be impossible

  2. Long leases slow recovery

  3. Short leases create false failover

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From visibility timeout/redelivery to generation-bound attempts, unknown-state handling and effect-specific duplicate protection.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Re-dispatch is safe even if the prior actor resumes; the mechanism is fencing, semantic idempotency or explicit compensation.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A visibility timeout or heartbeat is not proof the old worker cannot act.

WORKFLOW_STATE_PROPERTY

P27 — Completion defined by durable state plus verified postcondition
PROPERTY_ID

P27

PROPERTY_NAME

Completion defined by durable state plus verified postcondition

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

End-to-end correctness, transaction commit semantics, sagas and durable workflow systems.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  3. CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING

ORIGINAL_FORM

A distributed action is complete only at a declared consumer-relevant postcondition, not merely because a worker returned.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Workflow state says DONE while downstream, external or physical state is absent, stale or later rolled back.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Worker report, orchestrator commit and external observation occur in different failure domains.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

False terminal state, premature notification, duplicate re-execution and unreconciled real-world action.

MECHANISM

Define terminal invariant; persist transition; link required effect identities; independently query/observe or transactionally enclose them; record PARTIAL/UNKNOWN when not proved.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Completion drives user notification, billing, next workflow, resource release or irreversible decision.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Local transaction return covers the complete required postcondition.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Consumer-defined postcondition, authoritative evidence source, operation/effect identity, currentness and residual uncertainty policy.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes DONE auditable and meaningful, preserving uncertainty instead of hiding it.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Business process owner, caller, orchestrator and operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Worker report treated as effect proof

  2. Observation is stale

  3. External state changes after check

  4. Terminal state cannot be reopened

  5. One of several effects omitted

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Independent verification costs latency

  2. Some real-world postconditions are not exactly observable

  3. Continuous conditions can later become false

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From process return codes to durable terminal-state contracts with postcondition evidence and explicit uncertainty.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

DONE identifies the evidence and boundary establishing the required effect; otherwise state remains PARTIAL or UNKNOWN.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

Green task status is not completion.

P28 — Deterministic replay with explicit workflow/code version evolution
PROPERTY_ID

P28

PROPERTY_NAME

Deterministic replay with explicit workflow/code version evolution

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Event sourcing, replay-based workflow runtimes and durable-functions semantics.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. WORKFLOW_ORCHESTRATION_LINEAGE

  2. HYBRID

ORIGINAL_FORM

Re-executing orchestration logic against recorded history must reproduce compatible decisions, or migration/version logic must deliberately translate it.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Code, dependencies, nondeterministic APIs or schemas change while old histories are replayed.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Restarted orchestrator executes a different decision path from the one that produced persisted events.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Non-deterministic replay, stuck histories, duplicate task scheduling and semantic corruption after deployment.

MECHANISM

Restrict orchestrator nondeterminism; record decisions; version branches/patches; test old histories; migrate or pin incompatible workflows; separate external activities.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Replay-based durable workflow, event sourcing or state reconstruction across code versions.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Persist explicit current state without replay, or finish short-lived work before incompatible deployment.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Immutable history/event semantics, version identifiers, deterministic APIs, compatibility tests and migration/rollback plan.

FAILURE_MODEL

Worker/orchestrator crash, task redelivery, lease expiry, orphaned work, replay, cancellation race, code-version change and external side-effect uncertainty.

TIMING_MODEL

Timers, heartbeats and leases are policy evidence; they do not prove prior execution stopped.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Durable workflow state is distinct from correctness/currentness of external systems.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow run, task attempt and worker generation identify current ownership; stale effects are fenced or neutralised.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Activity dispatch is assumed duplicable unless the entire effect boundary is atomically closed.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

History/snapshot replay, versioning, unknown-effect reconciliation and manual intervention are retained.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Workflow state, task attempts, effect status and version are reconstructable.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Allows durable execution to survive code evolution without rewriting history accidentally.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Workflow/runtime developer, deployer and recovery operator.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Wall-clock/random call during replay

  2. Changed loop schedules new task

  3. Removed activity type

  4. Event schema incompatible

  5. Old binary unavailable for rollback

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Determinism constraints complicate programming

  2. Version branches accumulate

  3. External dependencies remain nondeterministic

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From replay assuming static code to versioned histories, compatibility APIs, migration and alternative speculative/current-state approaches.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

History, code and schema versions are explicit; every deployed version can replay or migrate all live histories.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'The engine replays deterministically' is not enough without code-evolution evidence.

P29 — Bounded queues with explicit work-age and capacity semantics
PROPERTY_ID

P29

PROPERTY_NAME

Bounded queues with explicit work-age and capacity semantics

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Queueing/service systems, staged event-driven architectures and production overload experience.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. OVERLOAD_AND_SERVICE_RESILIENCE_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

  3. HYBRID

ORIGINAL_FORM

A queue is finite deferred work against finite service capacity, not an infinite availability reservoir.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Acceptance continues after completion capacity is exhausted; backlog age and memory/storage grow until service or recovery collapses.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Producers and consumers scale/fail independently; queue hides demand from upstream while downstream saturates.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Unbounded memory/disk growth, extreme latency, expired work, recovery surge and hidden overload.

MECHANISM

Bound depth/age/bytes; attach deadlines and priority; reject/shed/spill according to consequence policy; size from service rate and recovery capacity.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Asynchronous buffering between independently varying producer and consumer demand.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Direct synchronous flow with natural backpressure, or small fixed local buffer where overload consequence is acceptable.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Measured arrival/service distributions, deadline/value policy, storage limit, drain/recovery capacity and rejection semantics.

FAILURE_MODEL

Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.

TIMING_MODEL

Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Makes queueing a deliberate latency/capacity trade rather than overload concealment.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Service owner, queue/stream operator, capacity planner and business owner.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Depth bounded but age unbounded

  2. Disk fills

  3. Old work no longer useful

  4. Priority starvation

  5. Backlog overwhelms dependency during recovery

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Hard limits reject work

  2. Burst absorption needs headroom

  3. Capacity estimates vary and can be wrong

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From unbounded buffering to multidimensional limits on count, bytes, age and consequence, tied to drain/recovery tests.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Queue admission is governed by the probability and value of completing work before its deadline, with explicit shed/defer behaviour.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'We put a queue in front' is not resilience.

P30 — Backpressure propagated to the source of demand
PROPERTY_ID

P30

PROPERTY_NAME

Backpressure propagated to the source of demand

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Flow control, bounded-buffer systems, stream processing and service-overload control.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. OVERLOAD_AND_SERVICE_RESILIENCE_LINEAGE

  2. EVENT_LOG_AND_STREAMING_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

A saturated consumer communicates a rate/credit/refusal signal upstream before queues and retries amplify demand.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Local queues fill while producers continue at an unconstrained rate; overload moves rather than resolves.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Each hop sees only local capacity and can amplify or buffer requests independently.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Cascading queue growth, wasted work, timeout storms and downstream collapse.

MECHANISM

Credit/rate/window control, demand signalling, concurrency limits, propagated deadline/refusal, or producer throttling across the dependency graph.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Producer can outpace consumer or fan-out multiplies work.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

In-process bounded channel or naturally demand-driven iterator when no remote graph exists.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Current dependency topology, demand accounting, admission semantics, retry integration and fairness policy.

FAILURE_MODEL

Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.

TIMING_MODEL

Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Aligns offered load with bottleneck capacity and stops overload migration.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Producer, intermediary, downstream owner and platform traffic controller.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Signal stops at one hop

  2. Retry bypasses backpressure

  3. Buffer masks saturation

  4. Control loop oscillates

  5. One tenant monopolises credits

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Coordination adds latency/state

  2. Topology changes

  3. Backpressure can reduce utilisation or create unfairness

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From hop-local flow control to dependency-aware end-to-end demand propagation and adaptive limits.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

Every admission path—including retries and async queues—consumes an explicit capacity signal that reaches demand origin.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

A local queue watermark with unconstrained upstream retries is not backpressure.

P31 — Admission control and load shedding with consequence policy
PROPERTY_ID

P31

PROPERTY_NAME

Admission control and load shedding with consequence policy

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

Overload control, queueing/admission theory and production service practice.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. OVERLOAD_AND_SERVICE_RESILIENCE_LINEAGE

  2. CLOUD_NATIVE_TRANSLATION

  3. HYBRID

ORIGINAL_FORM

Decline, degrade or defer work before accepted load exceeds the capacity needed to preserve critical service.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Systems accept every request and fail all of them slowly, or shed indiscriminately without preserving critical/fair work.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Capacity and demand vary across dependencies; overload signals arrive late and partial.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Overload collapse, tail amplification, critical-work starvation and invisible business loss.

MECHANISM

Concurrency/rate limits, priority and fairness, deadline-aware admission, graceful degradation and explicit rejection/deferral semantics.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Demand can exceed sustainable service or shared bottlenecks can saturate.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

Fixed small system with hard external demand limit and no shared saturation risk.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Capacity model, criticality/value classes, fairness policy, caller-visible rejection semantics, retry budget and telemetry.

FAILURE_MODEL

Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.

TIMING_MODEL

Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

P32 — Retry budgets, exponential backoff, jitter and deadline propagation
PROPERTY_ID

P32

PROPERTY_NAME

Retry budgets, exponential backoff, jitter and deadline propagation

HISTORICAL_ORIGIN

RPC retry practice, congestion/overload control and production guidance on coordinated retries.

LINEAGE_CLASS

  1. MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LINEAGE

  2. OVERLOAD_AND_SERVICE_RESILIENCE_LINEAGE

ORIGINAL_FORM

Retries consume bounded capacity and time; they are not free availability.

PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED

Every layer retries independently, synchronously and after the operation's useful deadline.

DISTRIBUTED_FAILURE_MODE

Partial failures/timeouts cause many clients to retransmit into a degraded shared dependency.

FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT

Retry storms, duplicate effects, wasted work, thundering herd and deadline overrun.

MECHANISM

Centralise/allocate retry budget; cap attempts; use exponential backoff with jitter; honour end-to-end deadline; retry only classified/transient/duplicate-safe operations.

TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT

Transient failure can plausibly recover within the remaining deadline and retry is semantically safe.

NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH

No retry for permanent errors, expired work, non-idempotent effect without closure or already-overloaded dependency.

DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS

Error classification, operation identity/idempotency, timeout distribution, downstream capacity signal, deadline and attempt accounting.

FAILURE_MODEL

Queue growth, shared bottleneck saturation, retry amplification, synchronized clients, head-of-line blocking, cascading failure and metastable positive feedback.

TIMING_MODEL

Deadlines and service-time distributions matter; old work may be worthless even if capacity eventually returns.

CONSISTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Consequence policy defines which work may be rejected, degraded, delayed or shed.

MEMBERSHIP_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS

Admission and priority policy has a defined owner; no implicit per-hop policy conflict.

DELIVERY_OR_IDEMPOTENCY_PRECONDITIONS

Retries preserve operation identity and consume an explicit budget; shedding has visible consequence.

RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS

Backlog drain, retry release and recovery surge are capacity-bounded and observed.

OBSERVABILITY_PRECONDITIONS

Queue age/depth, utilization, demand, retry rate, deadlines, drop reasons and dependency saturation are visible.

EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF

Retains availability benefit of selective retries without amplifying failure.

DECISION_OR_CONSUMER

Client library, service owner, workflow and traffic controller.

KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES

  1. Retries at every stack layer

  2. No jitter

  3. Timeout shorter than tail latency

  4. Retry after deadline

  5. Retry non-idempotent operation

  6. Hedging doubles overload

IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS

  1. Backoff delays recovery

  2. Error classification is imperfect

  3. Retries can hide systemic faults

HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED

From blind immediate retry to budgeted, jittered, deadline-aware and semantically qualified retries.

MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM

A retry is admitted like new work, consumes one end-to-end budget and carries the same operation identity.

CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY

'We use exponential backoff' is insufficient without attempt/deadline/idempotency/capacity bounds.
